bookTitle: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)

facts.statement: A futures contract is a standardized, binding agreement traded on organized exchanges to buy or sell an asset at a specified future date for a predetermined price.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)
sourceCitation.excerpt: Futures Contract: A binding agreement to buy or sell an asset at a specified future date for a predetermined price [1]. Futures contracts are standardized and traded on organized exchanges

facts.statement: A forward contract is an over-the-counter (OTC) equivalent of a futures contract, consisting of a non-standardized agreement between two private parties to buy or sell an asset at a future date for a set price.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)
sourceCitation.excerpt: Forward Contract: The over-the-counter (OTC) equivalent of a futures contract, consisting of a non-standardized agreement between two private parties to buy or sell an asset at a future date for a set price [3].

facts.statement: A company hedging an expected foreign cash outflow locks in its total domestic payment by multiplying the foreign payable amount by the forward offer exchange rate.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)

formulaDetails.name: Locked-in Forward Payment for Currency Outflow

variables.definition: Forward offer exchange rate quoted as domestic currency per foreign currency

numericalDetails.context: ImportCo locks in a payment of £10 million using a 3-month forward offer rate of 1.5742 USD/GBP.

facts.statement: A company hedging an expected foreign cash inflow locks in total domestic proceeds by multiplying the foreign receivable amount by the forward bid exchange rate.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)

formulaDetails.name: Locked-in Forward Cash Realized for Currency Inflow

variables.definition: Forward bid exchange rate quoted as domestic currency per foreign currency

numericalDetails.context: ExportCo locks in proceeds for £30 million using a 3-month forward bid rate of 1.5736 USD/GBP.

facts.topic: Lehman Brothers Leverage and Capital Vulnerability
facts.statement: Lehman Brothers reached a leverage ratio of 31:1 in 2007, making it vulnerable such that a 3% to 4% decline in asset values completely wiped out its corporate equity capital.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)
sourceCitation.excerpt: Leverage Ratio: Reached 31:1 in 2007... At a 31:1 leverage ratio, a modest 3% to 4% decline in asset values completely wiped out all corporate equity capital [16].

numericalDetails.context: Lehman Brothers bankruptcy on September 15, 2008, triggered by heavy subprime mortgage security exposure funded through short-term debt.

facts.topic: Post-2008 Regulatory Reforms for OTC Derivatives
facts.statement: Post-2008 reforms mandate trading standardized OTC derivatives on Swap Execution Facilities (SEFs), clearing them through Central Counterparties (CCPs), and reporting all OTC transactions to central trade repositories.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)
sourceCitation.excerpt: Post-2008 Reforms for OTC Markets: 1. Swap Execution Facilities (SEFs)... 2. Central Counterparties (CCPs)... 3. Trade Repositories [22, 23, 24].

facts.statement: Systemic risk is the risk that a default by a single financial institution triggers a chain reaction of counterparty losses, creating cascading failures across the financial system.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)
sourceCitation.excerpt: Systemic Risk Definition: The risk that a default by one financial institution triggers a chain reaction ("ripple effect") of counterparty losses, leading to widespread failures that threaten the entire global financial system [19].

facts.topic: Global OTC vs. Exchange-Traded Market Size
facts.statement: As of December 2014, the OTC derivatives market principal outstanding stood at approximately $630 trillion with a gross market value of approximately $21 trillion, compared to $65 trillion in exchange-traded underlying value.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)
sourceCitation.excerpt: OTC Market Principal Outstanding: $630 trillion [21] | Exchange-Traded Underlying Value: $65 trillion [21] | OTC Market Gross Value: ~$21 trillion [3]

numericalDetails.context: Comparative aggregate sizes of over-the-counter and exchange-traded derivative markets as of December 2014.

generalAssumptions: Forward and futures contracts eliminate exchange rate and commodity price risk by locking in delivery prices today.
Bank foreign exchange quotes apply the bid rate when the bank purchases currency and the offer rate when the bank sells currency.
Unregulated leverage leaves investment banks highly vulnerable to moderate asset price declines.
Novation by Central Counterparties (CCPs) mitigates systemic bilateral counterparty credit risk in OTC markets.
